title: staged-release-traffic-steering-scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick scratchpad for a staged rollout that uses traffic-steering + per-account pinning rather than a single global canary. Trying to reduce blast radius for high-risk model changes (kernel swaps / quantization / new tokenizer).

High-level plan (phases):
1) local dev + unit tests (already done)
2) internal smoke (team-only): 0% external, route 100% of test-account header to new variant for ~2h
3) gradual external ramp by account cohorts: 0.5% (low-value accounts) -> 3% -> 12% -> 40% -> 100% (decisions at each gate)
4) post-rollout watch window: 72h with sustained synthetic and production checks

Routing & pinning mechanics:
- Router will support two mechanisms (both implemented in router PR #214):
  a) header-based pin: x-rw-variant: <variant-id> (used for internal smoke and support repros)
  b) cohort hashing: hash(account_id + rollout_id) mod 10000 < threshold -> route to variant
- For high-sensitivity customers we will support explicit account-level pin via customer config (manual mapping stored in config-store).
- Ensure cookie / header precedence documented: header override -> account pin -> cohort-hash default.

Cache warming & KV concerns:
- Prefix/KV caches need explicit priming for model variant v2 because different KV keys (kv cache format change from kernel update). Plan:
  * Warm 50 warmup pods hitting priming endpoint with a curated prompt set (see "synthetic prompts" below) for 10 minutes before traffic shift beyond 3%.
  * Add a short TTL label on priming keys and plan for a key-format rollback key if we see cache mismatch errors.
- Avoid cross-model cache contamination: router must tag requests with model-variant id so cache namespace is segregated. Confirmed in PR but need integration smoke.

Observability gates (must pass before next step):
- Latency: p50 and p95 token latency increase <= 15% vs baseline for 30m during ramp-step.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx APIs <= baseline + 0.2% absolute.
- Quality guard: BLEU/ROUGE-style regression checks on the eval set: failure defined as >2.5% drop for any metric on primary prompt set.
- Cost guardrail: cost/token increase not > 30% sustained for 1 hour. If cost exceeds, pause rollout and investigate quantization tradeoffs.
- Infrastructure: GPU util for target pool < 90% and CPU steal < 5%.
- Alerting: create ephemeral slack alert channel (#rollouts-riley) and hook Prometheus alerts for the above thresholds.

Synthetic tests (minimal set for priming and ongoing checks):
- prompt-basic-short: 'Summarize: The product is a fast inference runtime.' -> expected keywords: inference, runtime, latency
- prompt-long-context: 5-paragraph input to test KV continuity -> assert no hallucinated footer, presence of prior topic name
- prompt-cost-check: short token-heavy prompt to track tokenization differences vs baseline
- Automated runner: run these every minute against both variants during ramp and compare diffs (use textual similarity heuristics).

Rollback playbook (fast path):
1) Move 100% cohort hashing back to previous variant via router control-plane toggle (rollback toggle + reason).
2) Drain new variant pods (scale to 0, keep logs & snapshots for 48h).
3) If rollback triggered due to cache mismatch, invalidate priming keys and force re-prime old variant.
4) Post-mortem owner: assigned to release lead (currently Riley S.). 48h initial incident report.

Communications:
- Internal: Slack - #rollouts-riley for live updates, #eng-release for bulletin. Post snippets at each phase change and on anomalies.
- External (if customer impact): Std customer comms template in Confluence (link above). Prep CS + AE playbook for manual account pinning.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we prefer account-level pinning for enterprise customers in phase 2 rather than cohort-hash? (Pros: lower noise; Cons: manual work -> ops burden)
- Need a smoke integration to verify KV namespace tags in staging (ticket REL-4029).
- Confirm whether the new tokenizer changes token count vs baseline for long docs (Dev to run token-diff suite).
- Decide runbook for graceful degradation: do we let router fall back to smaller model family if latency > threshold? (I lean yes, but must confirm legal for regulated customers).

Quick commands / snippets:
- force-route an account (dev CLI): rwctl route set --account 12345 --variant v2 --reason "support repro"
- toggle cohort percentage (admin UI): Admin -> Rollouts -> select rollout-id -> set percent 0.5 -> apply
- check synthetic diff locally: scripts/synth-runner --variant old, new --prompts synthetic_prompts.json --output diffs/

Notes to self:
- Keep a short log of which accounts we explicitly pinned during rollout to revert later.
- If we see small quality regressions tied to tokenization differences, try a vocab-only compatibility patch before full revert.
- Remember to update the onboarding doc for ops so next release lead doesn't miss the priming step.

References / useful links:
- router PR that adds cohort hash routing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/214
- rollout tracker: https://linear.app/RED/REL-4021
- cache-format discussion: confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/cache+format+change

End of scratchpad.

-- Riley
